As of 315 AM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Overcast, breezy, and unsettled conditions continue 
today.

Early morning surface analysis shows the broad Canadian high 
pressure still parked to our north with a wedge of cooler air 
extending down into our area. This wedge will allow for another day 
of cool, cloudy, and occasionally drizzly weather. Opted to lower 
high temperatures a couple of degrees today after yesterday's 
temperatures remained much cooler than expected, making the forecast 
show low to mid 60s inland with upper 70s for the east. There could 
be a few 70 degree readings in far SE VA and NE NC. The area of
low pressure off the coast will become more organized today and
strengthen before beginning to move NNE late tonight into 
Friday. This will allow more rounds of drizzle to move through 
today. Don't think we will see the widespread steady rain like 
we saw yesterday, but intermittent drizzle/light rain will be 
likely. Hi-res guidance has a lull for most of us from daybreak
through about mid-day before light rain chances increase across
the eastern CWA this afternoon. That pattern will continue into
the overnight hours as PoPs become confined to the Tidewater, 
NE NC, and the Eastern Shore. Strong NE winds will continue to 
create rough conditions for coastal locations through the day 
today. Gusts to 30-40mph are likely for all coastal areas, with 
the highest gusts up to 50mph along the Atlantic coast where a 
Wind Advisory remains in effect. Inland locations will see gusts
to 20-25mph. Dangerous surf, beach erosion, and moderate to 
major tidal flooding are all forecast once again today. Please 
see the sections below for further details. Low temperatures 
tonight will dip into the upper 40s for far western locations 
with upper 50s to lower 60s along the coast. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Drying out across the west on Friday, but rain
chances and gusty winds look to linger along the coast 
depending on the track of the low pressure system. Becoming 
drier and warmer next week. 

Latest 00Z model runs still show some slight disagreement in regards 
to the timing and future track of the coastal low Friday into the 
weekend. The ECMWF remains slower with the low and ultimately tracks 
it closer to the coast, eventually bringing the low along the 
NJ coast Saturday night into Sunday. The GFS is still a bit 
faster and further east with the low track through Saturday, but
has come ever so slightly more in-line with the ECMWF on Sunday
as it brings the low back to the New Jersey coast. Then they 
both have the low moving east out to sea by Monday evening. This
time frame is starting to come into the window of some of the 
higher resolution models like the NAM and the RAP, which are 
both a bit more closer to the GFS in keeping the low further 
offshore. Regardless, most solutions keep rain chances going 
along the immediate coast through the day on Friday, then 
shifting northward to be more confined to the Eastern Shore on 
Saturday, and just the Maryland Eastern Shore Saturday night 
into Sunday morning. This will also allow winds to remain 
elevated for coastal areas, though the direction will shift to 
become more northerly on Friday and northwesterly for the 
weekend. While it won't be quite as strong as what we're seeing
now, gusts to 30-35mph will still be possible. Winds should 
gradually subside through the day on Sunday as the low starts to
weaken and pull away from the coast. 

Another cool day is forecast for Friday with everyone topping out in 
around 70 degrees. Drier air will filter into inland areas allowing 
for overnight lows to dip into the lower 50s west of I-95 and mod to 
upper 50s to the east. The typical cooler spots across the far west 
may see upper 40s by daybreak Saturday morning. Temperatures then 
get noticeably warmer (but stay around average) as highs this weekend 
will be in the upper 70s inland. For the Eastern Shore where the 
cloud cover and rain may linger, expect highs in the lower 70s. 

High pressure builds into the region late Monday through Wednesday 
giving us a break with dry weather and sunshine. Temperatures will 
be able to warm more each day with the ridging overhead. On Monday, 
expect low to mid 70s for the north and upper 70s to near 80 degrees 
across the south. By mid-week, we may be well above normal once 
again (mid 80s) as southerly flow develops ahead of the next cold 
front. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...Widespread moderate to locally major tidal flooding 
(inundation of 2-3 feet AGL in vulnerable areas) will continue 
through at least tonight's high tide, with some degree of tidal 
flooding likely continuing through part of the weekend. Coastal 
Flood Warnings have been extended through Friday for much of the 
area.

Northeast winds continue to persist at 25-35 kt with gusts to 35-40 
kt (occasionally to 45 kt) early this morning. These winds are
